Trans Canada Bike Route (BC Only)

A ride described at Trans Canada Bike Route Network

How we describe routes →

Epic Expedition scale. Many demanding factors stacked, or 1,000 km and up, or 10,000 m of climbing.

Difficulty Our overall read of how demanding a route is. We score surface roughness, climbing, singletrack, and how far it runs from services. The route publisher's own rating, a lot of busy road riding, or sheer scale can push the tier up, never down.

Derived from OpenStreetMap. Good data, not perfect. Spot something wrong? Tell us.

How we describe routes →

The British Columbia portion of the proposed Trans Canada Bike Route, a national coast-to-coast cycling network still taking shape. The BC section maps about 5,400 km of connected riding, nearly all on paved roads, reaching from Vancouver Island through the southern Interior to the Cariboo. A planning framework and a dream to follow rather than a signed trail: expect ordinary highway conditions.

Fast-road stretches#

We believe these are the fast, unprotected roads on this route. We can tell you which roads and roughly how far, but not the order you will ride them. If you see an error, tell us and we'll fix it.

  • about 998 km of Yellowhead Highway · near Longworth
  • about 822 km of Trans-Canada Highway · near Munroe
  • about 690 km of Crowsnest Highway · near Mayook
  • about 292 km of Southern Yellowhead Highway · near Darfield
  • about 224 km of Island Highway · near Elk Bay
  • about 206 km of Kootenay-Columbia Highway · near Harrogate
  • about 123 km of Highway 3A · near Boswell
  • about 109 km of Lougheed Highway · near Nicomen
  • short stretches on other roads · 57 km total

Getting to this ride, bike and all#

Vancouver is the handiest transit doorway for this ride. The SeaBus, ferries, and buses will carry you and your bike there:

  • North Vancouverbest: SeaBus
  • Nanaimobest: ferry
  • Victoriabest: bus
  • Kelownabest: bus

🪶Traditional territories

The BC portion of this route travels through the traditional territories of the Á,LEṈENEȻ ȽTE (W̱SÁNEĆ), As’in’i’wa’chi Niy’yaw Askiy (Rocky Mountain Cree), Cayuse, Umatilla and Walla Walla, Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, Dakeł Keyoh (ᑕᗸᒡ ᗲᘏᑋ), Dënéndeh, Gitga’at Lax Yuup, Gitxaała, Gitxsan Laxyip, Halalt, Homalco, Hul’qumi’num Treaty Group, Hupacasath, Ĩyãħé Nakón mąkóce (Stoney), K’ómoks, Kitselas, Kitsumkalum, Ktunaxa ɁamakɁis, Kwakwaka’wakw A̱wi’nagwis, Kwantlen, kʷikʷəƛ̓əm, Lax Kw’Alaams, La̱xyuubm Ts’msyen (Tsimshian), Lekwungen/Songhees, Lheidli T’enneh, Liǧʷiłdax̌ʷ, ɬaʔamɩn gɩǰɛ (Tla’amin), ƛaʔuukʷiʔatḥ (Tla-o-qui-aht), MÁLEXEȽ (Malahat), Michif Piyii (Métis), Mountain Métis, Nadleh Whut’en, Nadut’en, Niitsítpiis-stahkoii ᖹᐟᒧᐧᐨᑯᐧ ᓴᐦᖾᐟ (Blackfoot / Niitsítapi ᖹᐟᒧᐧᒣᑯ), Nłeʔkepmx Tmíxʷ (Nlaka’pamux), nuučaan̓uuɫɁatḥ nism̓a (Nuu-chah-nulth), Nuxwsa’7aq (Nooksack), Qayqayt, Quw’utsun, S’ólh Téméxw (Stó:lō), sc̓əwaθenaɁɬ təməxʷ (Tsawwassen), Secwepemcúl’ecw (Secwépemc), Semiahmoo, səl̓ilwətaɁɬ təməxʷ (Tsleil-Waututh), Skwxwú7mesh-ulh Temíx̱w (Squamish), Snaw-naw-as, Snuneymuxw, snʕickstx tmxʷúlaʔxʷ (Sinixt), sq̓əc̓iy̓aɁɬ təməxʷ (Katzie), Stellat’en, Stz’uminus, šxʷməθkʷəy̓əmaɁɬ təməxʷ (Musqueam), sx̌ʷyʔiɬp (Colville), Syilx (Okanagan), T’eqt’aqtn’mux, Takla, Te’mexw Treaty Association, Toquaht, Ts’uubaa-asatx, Tseshaht, Tsuut’ina, We Wai Kai, Wei Wai Kum, Wet’suwet’en Yintikh, W̱JOȽEȽP (Tsartlip), Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ, and ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw-Askiy (Plains Cree).
